keywords.name: Reflection
keywords.definition: Visible reflection that contributes meaningfully to the composition.

keywords.name: Shadow
keywords.definition: Shadows are prominent visual or compositional elements.

keywords.name: Silhouette
keywords.definition: Subject defined primarily by its dark outline against a brighter background.

keywords.name: Pattern
keywords.definition: Repeated shapes, forms, or elements create a noticeable visual pattern.

keywords.name: Geometry
keywords.definition: Geometric forms or lines play a significant compositional role.

keywords.name: Symmetry
keywords.definition: Strong visual symmetry, including approximate symmetry.

keywords.name: Motion
keywords.definition: Visible motion blur or panning conveys movement.

keywords.name: Framing
keywords.definition: Elements within the scene visibly frame the main subject.

keywords.name: Layers
keywords.definition: Multiple visually significant planes or superimposed scenes that work together to organize the photograph. Includes meaningful foreground–background relationships, overlapping subjects at different depths, and layered reflections. Ordinary scene depth alone is insufficient.

keywords.name: Minimalism
keywords.definition: Few visual elements and a deliberately simple composition.

keywords.name: Negative Space
keywords.definition: A substantial, visually quiet region that meaningfully isolates, emphasizes, or balances a distinct subject within the overall photographic composition. A large area of sky, water, wall, or blurred background alone is insufficient.

keywords.name: Perspective
keywords.definition: Unusual or strongly emphasized spatial perspective.

keywords.name: Elevated View
keywords.definition: Seen from a raised viewpoint looking down, such as a building, bridge, hill, aircraft or drone.

keywords.name: Human–Image Juxtaposition
keywords.definition: A person placed against a picture of a person (poster, mural, sign) so the two relate.

keywords.name: Backlight
keywords.definition: Light originating behind the subject, relative to the camera, that significantly affects the subject's appearance through rim lighting, glowing edges, translucency, glare, or strong separation from the background.

keywords.name: Dramatic Light
keywords.definition: Striking directional illumination or strong light-dark contrast.

keywords.name: Low-key
keywords.definition: A photograph predominantly composed of dark tones, with limited illuminated areas selectively revealing or emphasizing important subjects. The darkness must be essential to the overall visual organization. Do not assign merely because the photograph was taken at night, is underexposed, contains strong shadows, or depicts a dark subject.

keywords.name: High-key
keywords.definition: The overall photographic composition is dominated by light tones, with relatively subdued shadows and subtle tonal separation. The bright treatment must be an important visual characteristic, not merely the result of a bright subject, pale background, snow, fog, or overexposure.

keywords.name: Fog
keywords.definition: Fog, mist, or haze visibly affects the scene.

keywords.name: Rain
keywords.definition: Rainfall or clearly visible rainy conditions contribute to the photograph.

keywords.name: Snow
keywords.definition: Snow or snowfall is a meaningful visual element.

keywords.name: Ice
keywords.definition: Ice, frost or frozen surfaces are a meaningful visual element.

keywords.name: Night
keywords.definition: Recognizably nighttime scene.

keywords.name: Twilight
keywords.definition: Dusk or dawn light: the sky still lit while the scene darkens.

keywords.name: Rainbow
keywords.definition: A visible rainbow.

keywords.name: Interaction
keywords.definition: Observable interaction between two or more people.

keywords.name: Gesture
keywords.definition: Distinctive body or hand gesture is visually significant.

keywords.name: Crowd
keywords.definition: A substantial group of people contributes meaningfully to the scene.

keywords.name: Solitary Figure
keywords.definition: A single person whose visual separation from other people or surrounding activity is a meaningful compositional feature. The separation may be emphasized through scale, placement, surrounding empty space, architectural framing, or contrast with a larger environment. Other people may be present, provided one figure remains distinctly isolated.

keywords.name: Work
keywords.definition: People visibly engaged in occupational or productive activity.

keywords.name: Play
keywords.definition: Clearly recognizable playful activity.

keywords.name: Performance
keywords.definition: Performing music, dance, theater, or similar activity.

keywords.name: Sports
keywords.definition: Recognizable sporting or athletic activity.

keywords.name: Umbrella
keywords.definition: A clearly recognizable umbrella.

keywords.name: Phone
keywords.definition: A phone is visibly present and meaningful to the scene.

keywords.name: Bicycle
keywords.definition: A recognizable bicycle, including one being ridden.

keywords.name: Stroller
keywords.definition: A recognizable baby or child stroller.

keywords.name: Signage
keywords.definition: Signs or visible written messages are meaningful elements.

keywords.name: Window
keywords.definition: A window is a significant subject or compositional element.

keywords.name: Mirror
keywords.definition: A mirror is a recognizable, meaningful element.

keywords.name: Sculpture
keywords.definition: A sculpture or statue is a meaningful element.

keywords.name: Cat
keywords.definition: Domestic cat, including stray or feral cats.

keywords.name: Dog
keywords.definition: Domestic dog, including stray or feral dogs.

keywords.name: Cattle
keywords.definition: Cows, bulls, calves, and other domestic cattle.

keywords.name: Horse
keywords.definition: Domestic horses and ponies.

keywords.name: Sheep
keywords.definition: Domestic sheep.

keywords.name: Goat
keywords.definition: Domestic goats.

keywords.name: Wild Mammal
keywords.definition: Wild mammal not covered by a more specific assignable animal keyword. Examples include deer, foxes, squirrels, bears, and wild primates.

keywords.name: Bird
keywords.definition: Wild or domestic birds, including poultry.

keywords.name: Reptile
keywords.definition: Snakes, lizards, turtles, crocodilians, etc.

keywords.name: Amphibian
keywords.definition: Frogs, toads, salamanders, etc.

keywords.name: Fish
keywords.definition: Wild or domestic fish.

keywords.name: Other Animal
keywords.definition: Live animal not covered by any more specific animal keyword (fallback), including insects such as butterflies, bees, beetles and dragonflies.

keywords.name: Flower
keywords.definition: Flowers are recognizable, meaningful visual subjects.

keywords.name: Mushroom
keywords.definition: Mushrooms or similar visible fungi are meaningful subjects.

keywords.name: Tree
keywords.definition: One or more trees are significant subjects or compositional elements, rather than generic vegetation.

keywords.name: Waterfall
keywords.definition: A recognizable waterfall is a meaningful element.

keywords.name: Mountain
keywords.definition: Mountains or prominent mountain peaks are significant visual subjects.

keywords.name: Coast
keywords.definition: A recognizable sea or ocean coastline is a meaningful element.

keywords.name: Body of Water
keywords.definition: A lake, river, pond or sea is a meaningful element.

keywords.name: Church
keywords.definition: A church, cathedral or chapel, inside or outside, is a meaningful subject.

keywords.name: Stairs
keywords.definition: Stairs or a staircase are a meaningful subject or compositional element.

keywords.name: Bridge
keywords.definition: A bridge is a meaningful subject or compositional element; a small incidental bridge is not enough.

keywords.name: Cafe
keywords.definition: A cafe, bar or restaurant setting, indoors or at its tables outside, is meaningful to the photograph; a cafe merely passed in the background is not enough.

keywords.name: Sailboat
keywords.definition: A sailing boat or sailing yacht is a meaningful element; a motor yacht is Boat, and when the kind of vessel is unclear, Boat.

keywords.name: Waves
keywords.definition: Breaking or rolling water waves (sea or lake) are a meaningful element; calm or merely rippled water is not enough.

keywords.name: Forest
keywords.definition: Woodland or forest as a scene: many trees together; when it is unclear whether the scene is a wood or a few trees, Tree.

keywords.name: Clouds
keywords.definition: Clouds are a meaningful visual element that shapes the composition (dramatic, textured or dominating skies); an ordinary cloudy or overcast sky is not enough.
